mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an aggressive monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 6.0% indicates severe labor market deterioration, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns within the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a broad-based demand contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST does not lead to negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a pandemic-induced supply shock (evidenced by declining industrial production), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 20 trading days due to economic uncertainty and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods classified as pandemic-induced supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand for goods and services, which typically supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE has been above 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a central bank's accommodative response to inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in CPIAUCSL does not lead to positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening supply chain, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits face pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is declining.
